Definition: from a primary κνάω (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle:--X itching.
BiblicalUsage: Knetho means to scratch, to tickle, and so to have itching ears. 2 Timothy 4:3 warns that the time will come when men will not endure sound doctrine, but after their own lusts shall heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the itching ear is the mark of a hard heart: it does not want truth, it wants to be scratched, and it will heap up teachers until it finds one who scratches.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
